35.author: St. John Chrysostom
35.work: Homilies on the Acts of the Apostles, Homily 45
35.text: At Miletus Paul gathers the elders of Ephesus for the last time and reminds them of a saying of the Lord that no Gospel records: it is more blessed to give than to receive. Chrysostom dwells on the fact that this is one of the agrapha, an unwritten word of Christ preserved in the apostolic memory. The saying is not less authoritative for being remembered orally; Paul preaches it to the bishops of Ephesus as their parting rule. The shepherd who gives more than he receives, who supports the weak, who refuses to make the priesthood a business, is the shepherd who walks in Christ's own footsteps.

35.author: St. Basil the Great
35.work: Homily on the Famine, On Riches
35.text: Basil quotes Acts 20:35 as the deepest reversal Christianity teaches against the assumptions of his age. Greco-Roman society held it more blessed to receive: gifts were owed to the strong from the weak. Christ overturns the order. The blessing of giving is not a sentimental reward for kindness; it is the structural truth of how the human person is made. The one who gives mirrors the God who gave the Son; the one who hoards mirrors no one but himself.
